meta_title: Pono — set it down, it holds
meta_description: The control room for agent-built projects. Your repository, database and hosting stay in your name.
access_request_body: Which project do you want to set down first?
hero_title_rest: Your app holds, and it’s yours.
hero_lede: Your agent writes the code. Pono holds the real state of every project and refuses what would break production. Your repository, database and hosting stay in your name.
hero_fine_rest: on your providers’ free tiers. No AI credits.
proof_refused_title: A migration drops a table in production.
proof_refused_body: Nothing ran. This refusal comes from the system, not from the agent.
problem_title: If you have to search for the answer, your projects aren’t being held.
problem_q1: You have several projects online. Which one is still running?
problem_q2: Which database is wired to which?
problem_q3: Who deployed last, and what went out?
benefits_title: The real state, the guardrails and your quotas, in one place.
benefit_state_title: Every project, as it really is
benefit_state_body: Environments, last deployment, links that work. Read from your providers, never typed by hand.
benefit_guardrails_body: Nothing ships without your approval. The refusal is mechanical: your agent cannot argue its way past it.
benefit_quotas_body: Your free tiers are watched. The alert arrives before your site stops.
mechanism_title: Your agent writes. Pono holds. Everything stays yours.
mechanism_intro: You stay in Claude, Codex or ChatGPT — the one you already pay for. Pono doesn’t resell intelligence: it holds the state and the rules.
mechanism_ready_body: No secret in the repository · preview checked · additive migrations. Only your approval is missing.
limit_not_editor: It isn’t a code editor: you stay in your agent.
limit_no_ai_resale: No AI resold by the meter.
faq_title: What people ask before setting a project down.
faq_for_me_answer: If you already build with an agent and your projects are scattered, yes.
faq_if_pono_stops_answer: Your projects keep running: they live on your accounts, not ours.
faq_why_not_replit_answer: Replit builds fast, and well. Pono holds what gets built, and doesn’t keep it.
faq_price_answer: A fixed price, never credits. Free tiers are enough to start.
cta_title: Which project do you want to set down first?
cta_body: Access on request while Pono is being built.

import_empty: No reachable repository. Add repositories to the Pono app installation.
connections_intro: Pono reads your providers and deploys nothing. Keys are encrypted and every use is traced.
code_host_body: Install the Pono app on the repositories you choose, then link it. No key is asked.

error_connection_provider_unsupported: This provider is not supported, or its address is missing.

error_service_chat_unconfigured: The service has no chat bot configured.

error_rollback_unsupported: The host can no longer go back to this version.

event_protection_unavailable: Protection not possible on this plan

error_oauth_access_invalid: This access is not possible for this request.
error_agent_grant_not_found: This agent no longer has access.
error_agent_scope_insufficient: This agent only has read access.

verdict_rollback_requested: An agent asks to roll {name} back.
verdict_rollback_requested_body: Nothing changed in production. Confirm or dismiss the request on the project; without an answer it expires in 24 hours.
rollback_request_body: Asked {when}. Production has not moved: only your confirmation brings the previous version back.
agents_intro: Agents linked to your workshop see and do what you do here, except approving a release or running a rollback. Cutting an access takes effect at once.
consent_access_read_body: Projects, releases and guards, evidence journal, importable repositories.
consent_access_act_body: Also: import a project, request a reading or an evaluation, protect production, ask for a rollback.
consent_never: Never, whatever the access: approve a release, or run a rollback without your confirmation. Every action is written to the journal with the agent’s name.
consent_sign_in_body: Sign in to decide. You will come back here, to the same request.
consent_missing: No access request in this link.
privacy_title: What Pono reads, keeps, and never does
privacy_intro: This page only describes what Pono really does today. Each sentence ties to a proof in our truth register.
privacy_reads_identity: Your code host (GitHub) login and, if you allow it, your email address.
privacy_reads_code: In the repositories where you install the Pono app: the list of repositories, the project manifest, change proposals and their changed files, for the guards.
privacy_reads_hosting: At your hosts and database (Netlify, Coolify, Neon): deployments, addresses and quotas, with the keys you add.
privacy_keeps_facts: The state of your projects, the guards’ verdicts and an evidence journal no one can rewrite.
privacy_keeps_keys: Your provider keys, encrypted; they are erased when you cut the connection.
privacy_keeps_tokens: Digests of your sessions and of your agents’ access, never the tokens themselves.
privacy_keeps_place: Pono’s database is hosted in the European Union (Frankfurt).
privacy_never_secrets: Keep the value of a secret found in a change: the verdict flags it without storing its value.
privacy_never_code: Copy your code out of your repository.
privacy_never_other: Show your data to another organization.
privacy_never_sell: Sell or hand over your data.
privacy_agents_body: An agent reaches your workshop only after your consent, given in the console. It sees what you see, never approves a release, and each of its actions is written to the journal with its name. You cut its access in one click.
privacy_remove_body: Cut your agents and connections in the console: keys are erased and the app is removed. To delete everything Pono keeps about your organization, write to the address below; the author does it by hand.

error_runtime_not_ready: The runtime is not ready yet.
error_runtime_unreachable: The runtime does not answer: nothing was written.
error_runtime_path_refused: This path is outside the project or protected.
error_runtime_files_refused: The runtime files proposal was closed without merging.
error_runtime_stopped_by_host: The server stopped the runtime (memory exceeded or failed to start).

verdict_runtime_failed_body: The reason is on the project. Nothing touched production.
verdict_runtime_save_conflict: Writes of {name} wait for a decision.
verdict_runtime_save_conflict_body: The development branch changed the same files. Nothing was overwritten: read them, then write the version you want.
event_runtime_changes_saved: Writes saved to the development branch
runtime_intro: Your application runs on your server, on the development database. Your agent writes, the screen changes in seconds, and every write is saved to the development branch — never to production.
runtime_limits: {started} of {max} runtimes started · 1 GiB each · sleeps after {minutes} min
runtime_proposal: Merge the runtime files proposal into {branch}: Pono then creates the runtime on your server.
runtime_conflicts: These files changed on the branch while the runtime was changing them. Nothing was overwritten: read them, then write the version you want.
runtime_file_title: Write a file without an agent
runtime_file_intro: The same gesture as your agent: the file applies at once, then goes with the next save.
